chunks: When the example of Mary's son is quoted before them, your people cry out at it,

key_terms.يَصِدُّونَ: They turn away / cry out in annoyance

ai.seo_question: Why did the Quraysh reject the example of Jesus (Isa ibn Maryam) as a proof of prophethood?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the Quraysh's irrational objection to Prophet Muhammad's humanity by contrasting it with their acceptance of Jesus' divinity despite his human attributes like eating and drinking. The term 'yassiddoon' (turning away) reflects their stubborn refusal to accept logical proofs, a theme emphasized by scholars like Al-Tabarsi who note the rhetorical force of citing Jesus as a 'masal' (example) to expose their inconsistency. This underscores the core Islamic principle that prophethood is not contingent on supernatural physical traits but on divine message and moral guidance.
